content:
Telegram 行政總裁 Pavel Durov has detailed the reasons behind the app's brief removal from the App Store last night. Here's what he had to say.

"I want to explain what happened and warn other app developers"

Last night, Telegram was abruptly removed from the App Store globally, without prior warning or explanation.

During the outage, many speculated the move was politically motivated, or in response to earlier discoveries that Telegram had been using obfuscated private UIKit APIs to animate its emoji selector.

Shortly after Telegram was reinstated, Apple reached out to 9to5Mac and explained that Telegram had actually been removed for CSAM-related violations:

Telegram responded to 9to5Mac, saying Apple "reported a user sharing CSAM content, who was immediately banned," and added that "in 2026, Telegram removed over 337,900 groups and channels related to CSAM."

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has now issued a more detailed statement about the incident, saying Telegram fell victim to a so-called "takedown blackmail" scam.

Here's the text of Durov's post:

🧹 Since Telegram promptly removes illegal content from public groups using various moderation tools, attackers resorted to technical tricks. Hackers edited an old message in an active group chat, injecting AI-modified illegal content. As a result, the content was effectively hidden from group members, preventing them from seeing it and reporting it in time. 💰 The attacker was a "takedown blackmailer": they extorted ransoms from group administrators, on the condition that their communities would not be targeted. Such blackmailers use automated accounts to plant illegal content in public groups and then report directly to Apple, attempting to get Apple to remove legitimate communities that refuse to pay.

Durov added that the blackmailer caused Apple to overreact, prompting Apple to remove the app from the App Store before contacting Telegram to resolve the issue. Durov said this "poses a potential systemic risk to every mobile app that features user-generated content."

He also noted that such "takedown blackmailers" are constantly refining their methods, threatening "communities on all major social platforms," regardless of how quickly or experienced those platforms are at handling similar incidents.
